about: What grows in Rome besides the trees of its squares and courtyards: the sacred groves (luci) that stood in the city from its beginning, the woods on the hills before they were built over, the orchards of the small city, and the pleasure gardens (horti) the rich laid out from the last century BC. Positions are map metres [east, north] of the Forum, radii too; 'from' and 'until' are years (negative BC). Kinds: sacred (oaks and a few cypresses, kept as a grove), wood (pines and oaks, thick), orchard (fruit trees in rows), horti (pines, cypresses, planes, box, flowers, a pergola or two, paths).

groves.name: the grove of Vesta
groves.note: Below the temple of Vesta, on the Palatine's slope: the grove into which the Vestals' hearth looked.

groves.name: the Asylum
groves.note: The saddle between the Capitol's two summits, where Romulus opened a refuge for whoever would come.

groves.name: the grove of Juno Lucina
groves.note: On the Cispian, the grove of the goddess of childbirth, older than her temple (375 BC).

groves.name: the grove of Libitina
groves.note: On the Esquiline, the grove of the goddess of funerals, where the undertakers kept their register of the dead.

groves.name: the Fagutal
groves.note: The beech grove on the Oppian, with the shrine of Jupiter Fagutalis.

groves.name: the grove of Strenia
groves.note: At the head of the Sacred Way: on New Year's day, boughs were carried from it to the Capitol.

groves.name: the grove of Furrina
groves.note: On the Janiculum's slope across the river, where Gaius Gracchus died in 121 BC.

groves.name: the grove of Stimula
groves.note: Under the Aventine by the river, where the Bacchanals met by night until the Senate put them down in 186 BC.

groves.name: the Caelian's oaks
groves.note: The Caelian was once the Querquetulanus, the hill of oaks, and its woods stood into the Republic.

groves.name: the Aventine's woods
groves.note: The Aventine outside the sacred boundary kept its woods, Diana's temple among them.

groves.name: the Esquiline heights
groves.note: The high ground over the agger, woods and the paupers' burial pits, until Maecenas made his gardens there.

groves.name: the Janiculum
groves.note: The ridge across the river, wooded to its top.

groves.name: the Quirinal's back
groves.note: The slopes behind the Quirinal and Viminal, still wooded in the small city.

groves.name: the Aventine orchards
groves.note: Figs and olives in rows on the Aventine's slope toward the Circus.

groves.name: the Esquiline orchards
groves.note: The market gardens and fruit trees at the foot of the Esquiline.

groves.name: the gardens of Pompey
groves.note: The planted walks behind Pompey's theatre: plane trees, fountains and statues, the first public park in Rome.

groves.name: the gardens of Lucullus
groves.note: On the Pincian, the hill of gardens: terraces, a great exedra, and the cherry trees Lucullus brought from Pontus.

groves.name: the gardens of Sallust
groves.note: In the valley between the Pincian and the Quirinal, the historian's gardens, imperial property after him.

groves.name: the gardens of Maecenas
groves.note: Maecenas laid them over the Esquiline's burial ground and the agger, with a tower Nero watched the fire from.

groves.name: the gardens of Lamia
groves.note: Beside those of Maecenas, and joined to them under Caligula.

groves.name: the gardens of Caesar
groves.note: Across the river under the Janiculum, where Caesar entertained Cleopatra, left to the people in his will.

groves.name: the gardens of Agrippa
groves.note: In the Campus Martius by his baths: a lake, a canal, and walks under the planes.

groves.name: the gardens of the Acilii
groves.note: On the Pincian's north, the gardens of a consular family.
